However, low-light images often suffer from amplified noise due to low photon counts and high system gain in camera sensors. Inspired by the physical priors of noise formation, we introduce the Noise Simulation Module (NSM) technique to simulate the noise distribution in nighttime scenes. Based on the shot-read noise model [12, 37, 40], we take the flare image as input and precisely simulate noise under low-light conditions in a physically decoupled manner. This approach ensures that the synthesized images closely resemble those captured in real low-light scenarios.
